newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil spills not disturbing shipping in Japan Sea.
newsitem.headline: Oil spills not disturbing shipping in Japan Sea.

text.p: Oil spills in the Sea of Japan have caused no serious disturbance in shipping operations, except to cause vessels in the area to take a roundabout route, a Maritime Safety Agency official said on Monday.
"We are not forcing them to keep away from the troubled area, but they are expected to avoid sailing into oil slicks just to be safe," the official said.

The Russian-registered Nakhodka, carrying 19,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil, broke up about 130 km (80 miles) off western Japan's Shimane Prefecture on Thursday, spilling an estimated 3,700 tonnes of its cargo.

The bow section of the ship, believed to contain 2,800 tonnes of heavy fuel oil, was spotted at about 45 km (28 miles) off central Japan's Fukui Prefecture at 8.15 a.m. (2315 GMT, Sunday), the official said.
